fixes.explanation: I wish it went that way, friend, but the text says the men of Israel fled. Many of them fell slain on Mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 31:1). This is a hard battle to read, so take it slowly. Holding the mountain isn't what happens here.

Saul isn't asking for a one-man stand, friend. He asks his armor-bearer to draw his sword and run him through. He says he's afraid the uncircumcised men will come and run him through and torture him. The archers had already wounded Saul critically. It's a heavy request, and the text doesn't make it lighter.

That's right, friend. The Israelites along the valley and across the Jordan saw that the army had fled and that Saul and his sons had died. So they abandoned their cities and ran away. That's what the text says, plain and simple.

Yes, friend. When the Israelites abandoned their cities, the Philistines came and occupied them. These are the same people who fought Israel on Mount Gilboa. The text says it plainly: the Philistines came and occupied their cities.

The Moabites aren't in the text here, friend. The Philistines are the ones who came and occupied the cities Israel abandoned. They're the same people who fought Israel on Mount Gilboa. The Moabites never show up in this chapter.

Yes, friend. The Philistines sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to proclaim the news in the temples of their idols and among their people. That's where the messengers announce it. The text names both places.

Not Jericho, friend. The text says the Philistines hung Saul's body on the wall of Beth-shan. Jericho never comes up in this chapter. Beth-shan is where the men of Jabesh-gilead went to retrieve the bodies.

Yes, friend. All their men of valor set out, journeyed all night, and retrieved the bodies of Saul and his sons from the wall of Beth-shan. When they arrived at Jabesh, they burned the bodies there. The text doesn't say why they went. I think this one is heavy, so let it be.

The text doesn't send them anywhere, friend. The men of Jabesh took the bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh. David isn't part of this scene. Burying them in Jabesh is what the text tells us.
